articles.body: 若手研究者のAIアクセス格差——構造生物学における一つの解、Meta Questというハードウェアから 私は今年の春、東京の狭いアパートの一室で、初めて「Meta Quest 2」を手にした。 当時、研究室のGPUクラスタはすでにフル稼働で、自分の分子動力学シミュレーションの結果を可視化するためのレンダリング時間が足りず、論文の締切に追われていた。 大学の共有サーバーにキューを投げても、帰ってくるのは「ジョブがキューイング中」という無表情なメッセージだけ。 そんなとき、先輩が「Questならスタンドアローンで 90 fps 出せるよ」と教えてくれた。 半信半疑で開封し、ヘッドセットを装着した瞬間、視界に広がったのは自分の作ったタンパク質の立体構造だった——まるでその分子の内部に潜り込んだかのような没入感。 なぜ Quest が「構造生物学の現場」で機能するのか 1. スタンドアローン GPU と低レイテンシ Quest 2 は Snapdragon XR2 を搭載し、オンボードで 6 DOF トラッキングと 90 Hz リフレッシュレートを両立している。 PC‑VR のように外部 GPU に依存しないため、研究室の共有リソースを占有せず、自席で即座にインタラクティブなセッションを開始できる。 # Quest 側で実行する最小限の Unity ビルド手順 $ unity -batchmode -projectPath ./ProteinViewer \ -executeMethod BuildQuest.BuildAPK \ -logFile - このスクリプト一つで、ChimeraX からエクスポートした .mol2 / .pdb をランタイムで読み込み、シェーダーで二次構造（α‑helix, β‑sheet）を色分けするアプリが 5 分ほどで完成する。 2.

articles.title: Building AI Senatus: Designing for Slow Deliberation When Drafts Arrive Instantly — What Worked, What Broke
articles.excerpt: Drafting used to be the slow part of policy. A proposal took weeks to write, and that delay quietly filtered out half-formed ideas. That filter is gone. A fluent, structured draft — definitions, phase…
articles.body: Drafting used to be the slow part of policy. A proposal took weeks to write, and that delay quietly filtered out half-formed ideas. That filter is gone. A fluent, structured draft — definitions, phased timelines, enforcement sections — can now be produced in seconds, and it arrives looking finished. Building AI Senatus, a public senate-style debate space for AI-drafted policy proposals, turned into a design problem about the other side of that change: if writing is instant, the product has to protect the slow part. Judgment is now the bottleneck, and most interface defaults work against it. What worked Treating polish as a risk signal, not a quality signal.

articles.title: From Fun Art to Finished Product: The Four Anti-Stall Scripts That Closed 36 of 39 Gaps**
articles.excerpt: I still have the screenshot of the rejection. Adobe Stock bounced a batch of 12 vectors because my CSV header had five columns and I'd given it four. No explanation, just a red error at the top of the…
articles.body: I still have the screenshot of the rejection. Adobe Stock bounced a batch of 12 vectors because my CSV header had five columns and I'd given it four. No explanation, just a red error at the top of the upload page. I'd spent two days generating the art. The upload took ninety seconds to fail. That was the moment I stopped treating my pipeline like a hobby and started treating it like a register. Every failure got written down. Over the following weeks I logged 39 distinct gaps between "I made art" and "this is a sellable product", and I closed 36 of them with four boring Python scripts. Here is what actually worked. Metadata is a formatting test, not a creative one The stock platforms do not read your CSVs the way a human does. Adobe expects a five column header. Vecteezy expects four.
articles.author: Muhamad Revanza Rafif Hamdani

articles.title: Shipping 39 Packaged Products with Only Pillow and reportlab: A Batch Pipeline Starter Kit**
articles.excerpt: Last March I lost six hours of batch uploads because of one CSV header. I had 240 JPGs ready for Adobe Stock, generated the metadata file with a script I'd written the night before, and the uploader r…
articles.body: Last March I lost six hours of batch uploads because of one CSV header. I had 240 JPGs ready for Adobe Stock, generated the metadata file with a script I'd written the night before, and the uploader rejected every row. The reason was boring: I had six columns instead of five. Adobe's upload CSV takes exactly five columns in a fixed order. Vecteezy takes four. Dreamstime takes fifteen. There is no partial credit. That night I rewrote the metadata script to hard-code the headers instead of "building" them, and it has not failed since. That rewrite is now one of four scripts I want to talk about, because the metadata CSV was only the first wall I hit. The four things that actually stall a solo pipeline Making the art is the fun part and it is maybe 20 percent of the work.

articles.title: Aegis Pulse: Exploring What a Camera Can Tell Us About the Human Body
articles.excerpt: What I Built I've always been curious about how far we can push technology beyond what it was originally designed to do. We use cameras every day to take pictures, record videos, and make video calls.…
articles.body: What I Built I've always been curious about how far we can push technology beyond what it was originally designed to do. We use cameras every day to take pictures, record videos, and make video calls. But what if that same camera could help us understand signals from the human body without needing to wear a device? That question caught my attention. When I discovered the Presage SmartSpectra SDK, I wanted to explore what was actually possible. I didn't want to just read about it or run a quick example. I wanted to build something I could interact with, experiment on, and learn from. That's how Aegis Pulse started. I built a macOS desktop application using Electron, React, TypeScript, and the SmartSpectra SDK to explore contactless pulse and breathing measurements.

articles.title: The model card is the model: a 3.7 KB PDF that classifies SMS
articles.excerpt: The model card is the model: a 3.7 KB PDF that classifies SMS Most model cards describe a model that lives somewhere else. This one carries the weights The artifact is a one-page PDF, 3,769 bytes. The…
articles.body: The model card is the model: a 3.7 KB PDF that classifies SMS Most model cards describe a model that lives somewhere else. This one carries the weights in its metadata. The artifact is a one-page PDF, 3,769 bytes . The visible page is a model card. The classifier is a 160-word Complement Naive Bayes with 1,579 bytes of int8 weights, stored as base64url JSON after /Keywords in the PDF's Info dictionary. pdf.html fetches the raw PDF, reads that string and runs the classifier in the browser. No server, no weights endpoint. It scores 93.54% on 1,115 held-out SMS messages from the SMS Spam Collection. Demo: https://byjameson-mini-ai.static.hf.space/pdf.html PDF: https://byjameson-mini-ai.static.hf.space/model-card.pdf Why a PDF A PDF is a document people already send to each other.

articles.title: Batch normalization, visually: the reset that keeps deep networks steady
articles.excerpt: Deep Learning, Visually #20 Watch the Short: youtube.com/shorts/yYxpjlvW69s A deep network is a chain of layers. Each layer takes a weighted sum of the activations from the layer before it, passes tha…
articles.body: Deep Learning, Visually #20 Watch the Short: youtube.com/shorts/yYxpjlvW69s Why the numbers drift A deep network is a chain of layers. Each layer takes a weighted sum of the activations from the layer before it, passes that sum through an activation function, and hands the result to the next layer. Training changes the weights at every step. So every layer keeps seeing inputs that have shifted since the last step: a new average, a new spread. In a deep network, those shifts pile up. With a big learning rate, the numbers can drift so far that they blow up, and training dies. What batch norm does Batch normalization adds a reset after each layer. For each neuron, over the mini-batch, it does three things: It finds the average (μ_B) and the spread (σ_B) of the neuron's weighted sums.

articles.title: SpaceX will launch epic double-catch Starship Flight 15 test mission on Nov. 13
articles.excerpt: SpaceX's next Starship test flight will take place on Friday (Nov. 13), and it will be epic: The company will try to catch both of the vehicle's stages when they return to Earth.
articles.body: SpaceX will make spaceflight history this week, if all goes according to plan. The company announced over the weekend that it's targeting Friday (Nov. 13) for the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket, which will attempt something that's never been done before. "The upcoming flight is planned to be the first to return both Starship and Super Heavy to the launch site for catch," SpaceX wrote in a description of Flight 15 . "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket." SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 14th test flight on Sept. 28, 2026.

articles.title: Meteorite that landed in Cape Cod was a 'lone wolf' from the outer solar system, scientists find
articles.excerpt: A meteor that exploded into fragments that fell into Cape Cod Bay was once part of the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, scientists found.
articles.body: Thanks to a combination of radar, infrasound, dash-cam and security camera footage, astronomers have tracked the bright daytime meteor that fell over Cape Cod Bay in May 2026 back to its origin as a small asteroid perturbed by Jupiter and sent on a comet-like orbit towards Earth. Meteor fireballs visible in the daytime are referred to as 'bolides'. At 1:06 p.m. local time (18:06 UTC) on May 30, 2026 one such bolide was widely witnessed falling out of the sky over coastal Massachusetts, with members of the public also reporting an associated sonic boom that rumbled across the north-eastern coast of the United States.

articles.body: This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on countries to commit to ensuring that AI is designed, powered, and deployed in ways that support climate action.
